task.description: Final re-gate (rework 3 of 3, budget exhausted) of WF-03 for ISS-0418, per ORCH's dispatch: attack the AC1->AC4 merge and the AC5 string-replay conversion for coverage loss, spot-check two of the six irreducible dispatches, verify the OQ-E measurement gate is concretely enforceable, and confirm S0/S6/S6.1/S6.3.1 tell one consistent conditional story.

result.summary:
PASS, with four MINOR findings recorded, none of which cost real coverage or make the measurement gate unenforceable. This is a materially different design than either prior gate reviewed -- the sequential-exhaustion BLOCKER from the prior re-gate is resolved not by hand-waving but by an honest two-part response (footprint reduction as far as it can honestly go, PLUS a real measurement gate for the residual uncertainty), and both parts hold up under direct re-derivation against real test source, not the design's own narrative.

=== a. THE AC1-TO-AC4 MERGE (design section 6.3.1 item 1) ===

Read both tests in full. AC1 (plugin_handler_test.exs:353-378, prior to deletion) asserts exactly four things against its own `req170_hang.wat`/500ms dispatch: (1) `{:error, reason} = result`, (2) `is_binary(reason)`, (3) `elapsed_ms < 10_000`, (4) `CallTimeout.classify(result) == :wall_clock_timeout`. AC4 (plugin_handler_test.exs:472-509, as it exists TODAY, unmodified) asserts on its own first (300ms) dispatch only: `{:error, _} = short_result` (reason discarded, never bound) and `short_elapsed_ms < long_elapsed_ms` (a RELATIVE comparison, not an absolute `< 10_000` bound) -- it never calls `is_binary/1` on the reason and never calls `CallTimeout.classify/1` anywhere in its body.

So THREE of AC1's four assertions (`is_binary(reason)`, the absolute `elapsed_ms < 10_000` bound, and the `classify/1` call) do NOT already exist in AC4's current test body -- the design's own §6.3.1 phrasing ("AC1's four assertions can be checked against AC4's own short_result/short_elapsed_ms values with no new dispatch... AC4's own test already produces as a byproduct") is loosely worded enough to read, on a careless implementation, as "these assertions already exist, just delete AC1." THIS WOULD BE A REAL COVERAGE LOSS IF THAT READING WERE FOLLOWED. However, re-reading §6.2 (not §6.3.1) resolves this: §6.2 line ~623-627 is EXPLICIT and DIRECTIVE, not descriptive -- "row 7's FIRST dispatch NOW ALSO CARRIES row 5's own four assertions... checked against that same dispatch's already-captured short_result/short_elapsed_ms" -- this is an instruction to ADD the three missing assertions to AC4's body against data AC4's dispatch already produces (the raw `short_result`/`short_elapsed_ms` values are genuinely already captured; only the additional assertion lines themselves need writing, which costs zero new dispatch). Read together, §6.2 controls the actual implementation instruction and it does not lose coverage. FINDING (MINOR, not MAJOR): §6.3.1's own phrasing in isolation is loose enough to be misread as "nothing to add," and a future reader who reads only §6.3.1 (as this validation initially did, before cross-checking §6.2) could implement this as a silent coverage loss. This is a real ambiguity risk, not a theoretical one, but it is RESOLVED by §6.2's own explicit text elsewhere in the same document, so no coverage is actually lost by a implementer who reads the whole design -- recorded as MINOR because the fix (tightening §6.3.1's own wording to match §6.2's explicit instruction) is wording, not a design defect.

=== b. THE AC5 STRING-REPLAY CONVERSION (design section 6.3.1 item 2) ===

Read the cited precedent directly: call_timeout_test.exs:113-139 is confirmed real and is genuinely the same TECHNIQUE (a `captured_reason` string literal, comment-documented as captured verbatim from one real run, asserted through `CallTimeout.classify/1` with zero live dispatch) -- not merely superficially similar. Confirmed this precedent's own captured string is the INNER-timeout shape (`"plugin handler ... crashed: {:timeout, {GenServer, :call, ...}}"`), while the test being converted (call_timeout_test.exs:155) exercises the DIFFERENT, OUTER-timeout shape (`"...did not respond within Nms"`, `plugin_interface.ex:223`'s own `nil`-clause construction). The design's own text is precise about this -- it proposes capturing a NEW string, not reusing the line-113 capture, applying the SAME LEVER to a different shape, not literally replaying the same data. This claim holds exactly as stated.

Checked whether the two dispatches the design cites as the ongoing live source for that string (plugin_handler_test.exs:152 [AC5] and :393 [AC3]) both actually produce it. Row 152 CONFIRMED: `assert reason =~ "did not respond within 100ms"` (line 165) -- this is a direct, live, unambiguous production of the exact string shape via `PluginInterface.invoke/3`'s real `handle_yield_result/4` nil-clause. Row 393 NOT CONFIRMED for this specific role: read the test in full (lines 393-430) -- it never calls `PluginInterface.invoke/2,3` at all (§6.2's own Shape B description is correct on this point), it reimplements `Task.Supervisor.async_nolink/2` + `Task.yield/2` + `Task.shutdown(task, :brutal_kill)` manually and asserts `yield_result == nil` and `refute Process.alive?(task.pid)` directly -- it NEVER constructs or asserts against the `{:error, "...did not respond within..."}` string tuple at all, because it never calls the `handle_yield_result/4` clause that builds it. FINDING (MINOR): the design over-attributes coverage by naming row 393 as one of "two other dispatches" that produce this string live -- only row 152 actually does. This does not cost real coverage (row 152 alone is sufficient as the live capture source the conversion needs), but the design's own precision about WHICH dispatch does WHAT is imperfect in exactly the place a merge decision is resting weight on it. Recorded as MINOR since the actual technique and the actual available live source (row 152) are both real and sufficient -- only the attribution to a second, non-producing dispatch is inaccurate.

=== c. THE SIX IRREDUCIBLE DISPATCHES -- SPOT-CHECKED TWO AGAINST REAL SOURCE ===

AC2 (call_timeout_test.exs:76, 2 dispatches): re-read in full. Confirmed genuinely irreducible -- this is the canonical live-verification test for req170's own central divergence finding (wasmex's documented interrupt-and-keep-Store claim is false), the second call deliberately reuses the SAME wedged pid (not an independent admission event, consistent with §6.2's own documented non-lease-wrapping exception for this exact call), and no other test in the suite dispatches via raw Wasmex.call_function/4 against this exact wedged-Store-reuse shape. The design's own justification is accurate.

AC3 (plugin_handler_test.exs:393, 1 dispatch): re-read in full (see part b above). Confirmed genuinely irreducible on its OWN stated ground -- it is the sole test proving the outer bound fires independently of a deliberately-LONGER inner bound (60,000ms configured, 500ms outer), and the sole Shape B (task-pid-observable) dispatch in the suite. This ground is real and distinct from any other test's claim, independent of part b's finding that this same test does NOT ALSO serve as a string-capture source (a different property than the one the irreducibility argument rests on).

Both spot-checks confirm the stated per-dispatch justification is accurate for what each dispatch actually claims to prove, distinct from part b's narrower finding about a DIFFERENT claimed role (string-capture source) layered on top of AC3's own irreducibility argument.

=== d. THE MEASUREMENT GATE (OQ-E / section 6.3.1's "Required verification") ===

Concretely specified: names the exact method (`:erlang.system_info(:logical_processors_available)` or `nproc`, run INSIDE an actual `mix test --only wasm_hang`-shaped job on the real target runner -- not inferred from vCPU count, the exact failure mode of the prior two gates), a precise numeric threshold ("strictly greater than 6"), and two named, mutually exclusive, fully-specified outcomes: >6 permits the unqualified "fixes the flake" claim WITH the measured number cited as evidence; <=6 requires escalation back through the design's own decision points rather than a silent merge, with two named fallback paths (push reduction further, accepting a fresh design decision on AC2/AC4's argued floors; or ship honestly as a partial fix and let ORCH decide). Confirmed the diagnostic infrastructure this gate leans on is real, not invented for this design: `scripts/test_parallel.sh`'s own `test_parallel: N=4 (source: nproc)` output line is a genuine, already-existing artifact in this codebase (confirmed via grep of `lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex:112`'s own regex matching that exact line format), so the gate is executable with existing tooling, not a hypothetical mechanism. This cannot be satisfied by an implementer merely asserting "looks fine" -- it names a specific command and a specific number to compare against, and explicitly forbids merging with the unqualified claim on the unfavorable branch. FINDING (MINOR): the gate is phrased as an obligation on "ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-RUNNER" generically without naming which specific WF-03 step or handoff must carry out the measurement before Step Final -- every other gate in this pipeline is pinned to a named step; this one is pinned only to "before merging... with an unqualified claim," which is still directionally enforceable (whichever agent reaches Step Final must check it) but is a softer procedural anchor than this pipeline's other gates use. Does not block PASS since the substantive threshold/method/escalate-instruction are all present and unambiguous; only the step-assignment mechanics are underspecified.

=== e. CONSISTENCY ACROSS S0/S6/S6.1/S6.3.1 ===

Re-read all four locations. All four now tell the same conditional story: §0's headline ("CLOSES the isolated mix test --only wasm_hang CI flake's own documented CONCURRENT-contention failure mode" -- carefully scoped to CONCURRENT-contention only, immediately followed by "this alone was found... to be insufficient by itself" and the GATED claim); §6's own section title ("...with the footprint reduced and the final claim measurement-gated"); §6.1's table (states AS-FOUND vs. AFTER-REDUCTION counts explicitly, 8 vs 6, with the reduction's own limits stated); §6.3.1 (the full gated-claim mechanics). No location found that asserts or implies the flake is unconditionally closed -- every claim of closure is explicitly scoped to the concurrent-contention mechanism only, with the sequential-exhaustion risk consistently named as open pending measurement, in all four places. PASS, no finding.

=== f. ITEMS NOT RE-LITIGATED ===

DetermInism claim's concurrent half, default-cap arithmetic, three call shapes, four production-uncapped locations, lease placement, monitor mechanics, new-primitive argument: no evidence rework 3 touched any of these beyond the already-reviewed §5.5/§6 areas; spot-read confirms §2/§3/§5/§7/§8 are textually unchanged from the already-passed rework-2 content. Not re-derived from scratch, per this gate's own instruction.

=== VERDICT RATIONALE, GIVEN GRADING INSTRUCTIONS ===

Per ORCH's own grading instruction for this final gate: reserve BLOCKER/MAJOR for something that would ship broken or claim more than it delivers. Both attacks in (a) and (b) found real imprecision in the design's OWN reasoning text, but in both cases the actual controlling instruction elsewhere in the same document (S6.2's explicit assertion-porting instruction; S6.3.1's own correct, narrower technique claim plus a genuinely-sufficient single live source at row 152) prevents the imprecision from costing real coverage or enabling a silent claim beyond what is delivered. The measurement gate is genuinely enforceable with a named method, threshold, and two hard-specified outcomes, and the consistency check found no location overclaiming closure. Four MINOR findings recorded per this project's own audit-trail discipline (do not silently drop a finding just because it does not block), none of which individually or together justify FAIL under this gate's own stated grading bar.

issues.finding: The prose describing the AC1-to-AC4 merge ("AC1's four assertions can be checked against AC4's own short_result/short_elapsed_ms values with no new dispatch... AC4's own test already produces as a byproduct") is loosely worded enough to be misread as "these assertions already exist in AC4's body, just delete AC1's test." Direct re-read of AC4's current test body (plugin_handler_test.exs:472-509) confirms three of AC1's four assertions (is_binary(reason), the absolute elapsed_ms < 10_000 bound, and the CallTimeout.classify/1 call) do not currently exist there -- only the underlying short_result/short_elapsed_ms DATA is already captured, not the assertion lines themselves. This is not a real coverage-loss risk because §6.2 (lines ~623-627) gives the explicit, controlling, directive instruction to add these assertions against that already-captured data -- but an implementer reading §6.3.1 in isolation, without cross-referencing §6.2, could reasonably conclude no new assertion code is needed. Suggested fix: tighten §6.3.1's own wording to explicitly state "the three assertions absent from AC4's current body (is_binary/1, the absolute bound, and classify/1) must be ADDED to AC4's existing dispatch, per §6.2's own instruction" rather than the current phrasing, which reads as though they are already present.

The design attributes live production of the outer-timeout reason-string shape ("did not respond within Nms") to TWO dispatches -- plugin_handler_test.exs:152 (AC5) and :393 (AC3) -- as joint justification for why converting call_timeout_test.exs:155 to a synthetic replay loses no live coverage of that mechanism. Direct re-read of :393 (AC3) confirms it never calls PluginInterface.invoke/2,3 at all (per §6.2's own accurate Shape-B description) and never constructs or asserts against the {:error, "...did not respond within..."} string -- it only asserts Task.yield/2 returns nil and the task dies, a different, real property but not this one. Only row 152 (AC5) actually produces this exact string live (confirmed: `assert reason =~ "did not respond within 100ms"`). This does not cost real coverage, since row 152 alone is a sufficient, genuinely-live capture source for the synthetic replay this conversion needs -- but the design's own claim of TWO independent live sources for this specific property is inaccurate; only one exists. Suggested fix: correct §6.3.1 item 2 to name only plugin_handler_test.exs:152 as the live source for the string-capture, and describe :393's role (if any) accurately as covering a different property (outer-bound-independent-of-longer-inner-bound), not this one.

The measurement gate names a method, a precise threshold ("strictly greater than 6"), and two fully-specified outcomes, but assigns responsibility only generically to "ELIXIR-DEV/TEST-RUNNER" and anchors timing only to "before merging... with an unqualified claim" rather than to a named WF-03 step/handoff the way this pipeline's other gates are pinned. This is a softer procedural anchor than this pipeline typically uses, though still directionally enforceable (whichever agent reaches Step Final must check it before claiming closure). Suggested fix, not blocking: name the specific step (e.g. TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 real-CI verification, or a dedicated Step 4b) that must perform and record this measurement, so it cannot be silently skipped by an agent who does not think to look for an un-stepped obligation.

Carried forward, unchanged, from the two prior gates: the original §8 code-shape sketch (wiring try_acquire/release inside handle_node/1) remains present verbatim, marked superseded by §8.1 rather than removed. Still not blocking -- the document itself clearly flags the supersession -- but recorded again per this project's audit-trail discipline since it was never actually cleaned up across three reworks.

result.next_action: PASS. Route to ELIXIR-DEV for implementation per WF-03 Step 3, carrying forward: (1) the design's own OQ-E measurement gate as a hard precondition before the implementation's PR/CI-verification report may claim this design 'closes ISS-0418's CI flake' -- if available_parallelism() measured inside a real ubuntu-latest mix test --only wasm_hang subprocess is <= 6, escalate to ORCH per the design's own two named fallback paths rather than merging silently; (2) this validator's four MINOR findings, which do not block implementation but should be corrected in the design doc's own text (or accepted as documented residual imprecision) at ORCH's discretion, since the rework budget for this design gate is now exhausted.
